title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: An agent answers a student's question in step 1 and is called again for step 2 of the same run. What does the model have available for step 2 beyond its fixed training?

options.text: Everything the program puts in the step 2 input
A private record of its own earlier calls in the run
Its step 1 reasoning, kept inside the model between calls
Every earlier conversation with every student it has served

items.stem: A run makes 5 model calls. The starting context is 1,500 tokens and each of the first 4 steps adds 500 tokens to the context. What is the total number of input tokens billed across all 5 calls?
Your assistant must know on Friday that a student passed the router training on Tuesday. Which design provides this?

options.text: Use a model with a context window large enough for a week
Save a record outside the model and load it each session
Tell the model in its system prompt to remember students
Retrieve it from the machine manuals using embedding search

items.stem: Students search the manuals for exact error codes such as "E-47". Embedding-only retrieval often returns pages about other errors. Which change most directly addresses this?

options.text: Add keyword (BM25) search and merge it with the embeddings
Raise the number of chunks sent to the model to forty
Rewrite the system prompt to say that codes are important
Switch to a model whose context window is much larger

items.stem: In one word: what is the name for asking the model to summarise a long conversation and replacing the old messages with that summary when the context nears its limit?
